paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Conceptualized and operationalized targets by year along with the distribution of datasets. Targeted refers to datasets that have explicitly mentioned at least one target in their construct definition (i.e., in the conceptualization phase) and/or publications in which the authors define concrete measures to ensure and validate the presence of at least one target group in the data (i.e., in the operationalization phase). Untargeted refers to all other datasets that do not meet these two criteria. Note that the data for 2022 is only partially available (as described in our Methods and Data Section).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets categorized as "Targeted" and "Untargeted" from 2012 to 2022, with the y-axis representing the "Number of datasets" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 160 in increments of 20, and the x-axis showing the "Year" from 2012 to 2022. Each year is represented by a stacked bar, where the lower portion (blue) corresponds to "Untargeted" datasets and the upper portion (orange) to "Targeted" datasets. In 2012, both categories have minimal counts, with only a small number of untargeted datasets. A gradual increase is observed from 2013 to 2016, with the number of targeted datasets rising slightly. From 2017 to 2022, there is a significant upward trend, particularly for targeted datasets, which grow substantially each year. By 2021, the number of targeted datasets reaches its peak at approximately 100, while untargeted datasets reach about 65. In 2022, the data is partially available, showing a total of around 40 datasets, with approximately 30 being targeted and 10 untargeted. The chart highlights a clear shift toward more targeted datasets over time, with the majority of datasets in recent years being explicitly focused on specific target groups.
